html:
Hafez al-Assad ruled Syria from 1970 until his death in 2000. He built a state around himself, his family and his Alawite community that lasted until 2024.

An air force officer from a poor Alawite family, he rose through the Ba'ath Party and the army. He lost the Golan Heights as defence minister in the Six-Day War of 1967, and seized power in 1970. He made Syria a strong state allied with the Soviet Union and Iran, fought Israel in 1973, and sent troops into Lebanon in 1976.

He ruled through many secret police forces. When the Muslim Brotherhood rose against him, his forces crushed the city of Hama in the 1982 massacre. His son Bashar succeeded him and lost power in the fall of the regime in 2024.
